'''Peter J. Nordlander''' is a Swedish physicist.

== Career ==
Nordlander completed a doctorate in theoretical physics at [[Chalmers University of Technology]]. Following postdoctoral research at [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]], [[Bell Labs]], and [[Rutgers University]], Nordlander began teaching at [[Rice University]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite news |title=Prof. Peter Nordlander |url=http://nordlander.rice.edu/members/nordlander |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Rice University}}</ref> He works within the Laboratory for Nanophotonics at Rice, and serves as the Wiess Chair and Professor of Physics and Astronomy.<ref>{{cite news |title=Light makes Rice University catalyst more effective |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2018-10/ru-lmr100318.php |accessdate=29 October 2019 |work=EurekAlert! |date=4 October 2018}}</ref>

== Research ==
Nordlander's research focuses on theoretical nanophotonics and plasmonics. He has collaborated extensively with [[Naomi Halas]] at [[Rice University]] on the development of plasmonic nanostructures and their applications in optics, sensing, and catalysis.<ref name="RiceProfile">{{cite web |title=Prof. Peter Nordlander |url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/peter-j-nordlander |website=Rice University |access-date=9 September 2025}}</ref>

Together with Halas and then-student Emil Prodan (now Professor of Physics at Yeshiva University), Nordlander developed the Plasmon Hybridization model. This theory explains the plasmonic properties of nanoparticles of complex shapes in terms of interacting primitive plasmon modes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Prodan |first1=E. M. |last2=Radloff |first2=C. |last3=Halas |first3=N. J. |last4=Nordlander |first4=P. |title=A Hybridization Model for the Plasmon Response of Complex Nanostructures |journal=Science |volume=302 |pages=419–422 |date=2003 |doi=10.1126/science.1089171}}</ref>

His group has investigated plasmonic nanocavities, nanoparticle dimers, and active optical antennas. These studies revealed symmetry-breaking effects, Fano resonances, and quantum plasmonic behaviors in metallic nanostructures.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hao |first1=F. |last2=Sonnefraud |first2=Y. |last3=Van Dorpe |first3=P. |last4=Maier |first4=S. A. |last5=Halas |first5=N. J. |last6=Nordlander |first6=P. |title=Symmetry breaking in plasmonic nanocavities: Subradiant LSPR sensing and a tunable Fano resonance |journal=Nano Letters |volume=8 |pages=3983–3988 |date=2008 |doi=10.1021/nl802509r}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zuloaga |first1=J. |last2=Prodan |first2=E. |last3=Nordlander |first3=P. |title=Quantum description of the plasmon resonances of a nanoparticle dimer |journal=Nano Letters |volume=9 |pages=887–891 |date=2009 |doi=10.1021/nl803811g}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Nordlander was elected to fellowship of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2002 "for pioneering contributions to the chemical physics of atom-surface interactions, including the development of a many-body theoretical description of charge transfer processes in atom-surface scattering."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=N&year=2019&unit_id=&institution= |accessdate=29 October 2019}}</ref> He is also a fellow of [[SPIE]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[Optical Society]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Peter Nordlander |url=https://spie.org/profile/Peter.Nordlander-17037?SSO=1 |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=SPIE}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Boyd |first1=Jade |title=Halas, Nordlander awarded Optical Society's R.W. Wood Prize |url=https://news.rice.edu/2015/03/19/halas-nordlander-awarded-optical-societys-r-w-wood-prize/ |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Rice University |date=19 March 2015}}</ref> Nordlander was one of three recipients of the Willis E. Lamb Award in 2013,<ref>{{cite news |title=The 2013 Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics |url=https://www.lambaward.org/2013/index.html |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Winter Colloquium on the Physics of Quantum Electronics/Lamb Award |date=9 January 2013}}</ref> "for pioneering theoretical contributions in the field of plasmonics"<ref>{{cite news |title=Peter Nordlander, Rice University |url=https://www.lambaward.org/2013/2013-nordlander.html |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Winter Colloquium on the Physics of Quantum Electronics/Lamb Award |date=9 January 2013}}</ref> alongside [[Shaul Mukamel]] and [[Susanne Yelin]]. Nordlander, [[Naomi Halas]], and [[Tony Heinz]] won the 2014 [[Frank Isakson Prize for Optical Effects in Solids]] awarded by the American Physical Society.<ref>{{cite news |title=Halas, Nordlander win American Physical Society's Isakson Prize |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/bellaire/news/article/Halas-Nordlander-win-American-Physical-Society-s-9571822.php |accessdate=29 October 2019 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=18 October 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=2014 Frank Isakson Prize for Optical Effects in Solids Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Peter&last_nm=Nordlander&year=2014 |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> Nordlander and Halas shared a second award in 2015, the Optical Society's [[R. W. Wood Prize]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ruth |first1=David |last2=Boyd |first2=Jade |title=Halas, Nordlander awarded Optical Society's R.W. Wood Prize |url=https://news.rice.edu/2015/03/19/halas-nordlander-awarded-optical-societys-r-w-wood-prize/ |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Rice University |date=19 March 2015}}</ref> In 2016, Nordlander was listed an [[ISI highly cited researcher]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Mike |title=9 Rice faculty on prominent 'highly cited' list |url=https://news.rice.edu/2016/11/18/9-rice-faculty-on-prominent-highly-cited-list/ |accessdate=29 October 2019 |publisher=Rice University |date=18 November 2016}}</ref>
